subject.title: [Bug]: Potential resource leak in runBoundTurnWithMissingThreadRecovery -- retry not wrapped in try/finally after thread spawn

question: Should Codex app-server conversation bindings keep a persistent subscription across bound turns, or should OpenClaw reattach before each turn and unsubscribe after each attempt?
rationale: The bug is real from source inspection, but the previously attempted broad unsubscribe fix can break later bound messages because Codex turn/start does not reattach the connection listener.

options.title: Persistent subscription with narrow failure cleanup
options.body: Keep normal bound conversations subscribed across turns and add cleanup only for replacement-thread retry failure paths that cannot affect later delivery.

options.title: Per-turn reattach and unsubscribe
options.body: Change bound turns to explicitly reattach or resume before each turn/start, then unsubscribe after each attempt with two-turn regression proof.

options.title: Accept current persistent behavior
options.body: Leave the source-level leak risk in place unless a live orphan-count reproduction demonstrates that cleanup is worth the delivery-risk tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Persistent subscription with narrow failure cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep normal bound conversations subscribed across turns and add cleanup only for replacement-thread retry failure paths that cannot affect later delivery.

likelyOwner.reason: History ties steipete to the recovery merge and adjacent Codex app-server lifecycle cleanup work, making them the best available routing owner for the lifecycle decision.
